chunks: 643 - It is narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام that he said:

A group of Jews came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and the most knowledgeable of them asked him about matters. Among what he asked was that he said: Inform me about Allah, Mighty and Majestic: for what reason did Allah, Mighty and Majestic, make these five salat (prayers) obligatory in five appointed times upon your Ummah during the hours of the night and the day?

So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: Indeed, when the sun is at zenith, it has a ring into which it enters, and when it enters it, the sun declines. Then everything beneath the Throne glorifies with the praise of my Lord, majestic is His majesty. It is the hour in which my Lord, majestic is His majesty, sends blessings upon me. So Allah made the salat (prayer) obligatory upon me and upon my Ummah in it, and He said:
Establish the salat (prayer) at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night.

And it is the hour in which Jahannam will be brought on the Day of Resurrection. So there is no believer who coincides with that hour while prostrating, bowing, or standing except that Allah will forbid his body to the Fire.

As for Salat al-ʿAṣr, it is the hour in which Ādam عليه السلام ate from the tree, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought him out from al-Jannah. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded his progeny with this salat (prayer) until the Day of Resurrection, and chose it for my Ummah. So it is among the most beloved prayers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He instructed me to preserve it among the prayers.

As for Salat al-Maghrib, it is the hour in which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, turned to Ādam عليه السلام in repentance. Between the time he ate from the tree and the time Allah, Mighty and Majestic, accepted his repentance were three hundred years from the days of the world, and in the days of the Hereafter one day is:

From al-ʿAṣr to al-ʿIshāʾ. And Ādam عليه السلام prayed three rakʿahs: one rakʿah for his sin, one rakʿah for the sin of Ḥawwāʾ, and one rakʿah for his repentance. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made these three rakʿahs obligatory upon my Ummah. And it is the hour in which duʿa (supplication) is answered, so my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, promised me that He will answer whoever supplicates to Him in it. And it is the salat (prayer) with which my Lord commanded me in His saying, blessed and exalted is He:
So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning.

As for Salat al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah, indeed the grave has darkness, and the Day of Resurrection has darkness. My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, commanded me and my Ummah with this salat (prayer) so that it may illuminate the grave and so that He may grant me and my Ummah light upon al-Ṣirāṭ. There is no foot that walks to Salat al-ʿAtamah except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbids its body to the Fire. And it is the prayer which Allah, exalted is He and holy is His remembrance, chose for the messengers before me.

As for Salat al-Fajr, when the sun rises, it rises upon the two horns of al-Shayṭān. So my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, commanded me to perform Salat al-Ghadāh before the rising of the sun and before the disbeliever prostrates to it, so that my Ummah may prostrate to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Its promptness is more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and it is the prayer witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.

key_terms.تَوْبَتِهِ: his repentance, referring to Ādam’s return to Allah
key_terms.جَهَنَّمَ: Hellfire, mentioned here in relation to protection through prayer
key_terms.مَلَائِكَةُ: the angels who witness the Fajr prayer
key_terms.مَوَاقِيتَ: fixed and designated times for acts of worship
key_terms.ٱلدُّعَاءُ: supplication, especially at a time when it is answered
key_terms.ٱلزَّوَالِ: the sun’s decline from its zenith, marking the time of Ẓuhr
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَوَاتِ: the prescribed daily prayers made obligatory at appointed times
key_terms.ٱلصِّرَاطِ: the bridge in the Hereafter over which believers are granted light

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah prescribe the five daily prayers at specific times?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the divine wisdom behind the obligation of the five daily prayers at their appointed times. It links each salat to cosmic realities, events in the life of Ādam عليه السلام, acceptance of duʿa, and protection in the Hereafter, while also citing Qur’anic verses connected to prayer times.
